newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA BEAT EXTREMADURA TO KEEP UP WITH REAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA BEAT EXTREMADURA TO KEEP UP WITH REAL.

text.p: Barcelona kept pace with Spanish league leaders Real Madrid ahead of next weekend's vital top-of-the-table clash between the two sides when they beat bottom club Extremadura 3-0 on Monday.
With 34 points from 15 games Barcelona are one point behind leaders Real, and one ahead of Deportivo Coruna.
Barcelona went ahead in the 13th minute through midfielder Giovanni who collected the ball from fellow Brazilian Ronaldo and gave Extremadura keeper Eduardo Almendro no chance.
Extremadura refused to be overawed and five minutes later put together a fine move which ended with Jose Soler being upended by Albert Ferrer.
The referee had no hesitation in awarding a penalty, but Juanito Rodriguez blasted the ball wide from the spot, and the visitors went on to waste several other clear chances.

Barcelona captain Gheorge Popescu made it 2-0 in the 40th minute after slipping his marker at a corner, and the game was sealed just before halftime when Giovanni sliced through the Extremadura defence and somehow kept possession despite stumbling.
As he moved to shoot the unfortunate Juanito knocked the ball into his own net.
Juanito was robbed of the chance to make amends at the end of an evenly-balanced second half when keeper Vitor Baia stopped a fierce shot with a superb reflex save.
